events.text: A minister of the Celestial Ministries asks you to carry a sealed decree to the Star Marshal of the East. On the road you learn what it says: the Marshal is to be stripped of rank, for a fault the minister invented. {b3_peer}, a junior officer of the Ministries, rides with you and has read it too.

choices.text: Deliver the decree as ordered

effects.log: You deliver it. The Marshal reads it, looks at you for a long moment, and says only: "So that is how it is up here." You rise in the minister's favour, and you do not enjoy it.

choices.text: Warn the Marshal first

effects.log: You warn the Marshal. The decree arrives anyway, but the Marshal is ready for it, and the minister never finds out who spoke. Some debts up here are paid in very long silences.

choices.text: Return the decree to the minister, unopened in spirit

effects.log: You hand it back. "Find someone else," you say. The minister smiles the smile of someone who has a very long memory. You will have to watch your step.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries are divided over whether to open the white stairs to more of the world below. Both factions want your voice. {b3_elder} leads one side; {b3_peer}, who came up the stairs the same century as you, leads the other.

choices.text: Speak for opening the stairs

effects.log: You speak for the stairs. Half the court stops speaking to you. The other half starts. A few more mortals will climb, one day, because you spoke.

choices.text: Speak for keeping them as they are

effects.log: You speak for the old way. It carries the day. You are not entirely sure you were right, and that doubt stays with you.

choices.text: Refuse to take a side

effects.log: You refuse. Everyone respects it; nobody trusts it. That is the court.

events.text: The Celestial Lord summons you to a garden where nobody else is allowed. "Every lord before me was betrayed by a minister," the Lord says. "Tell me who will betray me." Outside the garden gate {b3_peer} is waiting, and pretends not to be.

choices.text: Name the minister you know is plotting

effects.log: You name them. The minister is gone from court by morning, quietly, to a cloud nobody visits. The Lord trusts you now, which is its own kind of weight.

choices.text: Say that a lord who fears betrayal invites it

effects.log: The Lord is silent for a long while, then laughs. "You will be the one, then," the Lord says, "and I will never see it coming." You are given a seat closer to the throne.

events.text: Two elders of the Jade Void Sect have not spoken to each other in nine thousand years. Each sends you to deliver a message to the other. The messages contradict each other. {b3_peer}, who carried the last message nine centuries ago, wishes you luck.

choices.text: Deliver both, word for word

effects.log: You deliver both. Nothing changes, which is apparently what they both wanted. The sect respects a messenger who does not improve on messages.

choices.text: Bring them face to face

effects.log: You arrange for both to arrive at the same pavilion. They glare for a day, and on the second day one of them pours tea. The sect talks about it for a century.

events.text: A young sword immortal of the sect has stolen a technique from the sect's forbidden library, and confesses it to you alone. The library's keeper is {b3_elder}, who trusts you.

choices.text: Report it to the elders

effects.log: You report it. The young immortal is sent to guard the jade bridge for a thousand years. They will not forgive you, and the elders will not forget your loyalty.

choices.text: Help them return it before anyone notices

effects.log: You help put the scroll back, at night, on the exact shelf. Nobody ever knows. The young immortal will owe you, for a very long time.

choices.text: Ask what they learned from it

effects.log: They show you. It is a beautiful technique, and very dangerous. You keep the secret, and some of the lesson.

events.text: The Sect Ancestor of the Jade Void wishes to retire into the Void at last, and names three successors. You are one of them. There is to be a duel. {b3_peer} is another, and has been training for this since the day you met.

choices.text: Fight for the seat

ok.log: You win the duel for the seat and offer it at once to the eldest, who refuses it twice and accepts on the third time. You have become something the sect will talk about for an age.

fail.log: You lose the duel, cleanly, and bow. The new Sect Ancestor remembers how you lost, which is worth more than many victories.

choices.text: Withdraw in favour of the eldest

effects.log: You withdraw. The eldest takes the seat and gives you the second place beside it, which up here is a kind of love.

events.text: The seventh cloud of the Nine Clouds Palace is sinking. The palace masters blame each other's arrays. You are asked to find the fault. {b3_elder} drew the array in question, and is watching you read it.

choices.text: Find it, whoever it shames

effects.log: It is the eldest master's array, a single line drawn wrong ten thousand years ago. You fix it in front of everyone. The cloud rises; the master does not speak to you for a century.

choices.text: Fix it quietly and let nobody be blamed

effects.log: You redraw the line at night. In the morning the cloud is rising and every master thinks their own work saved it. Peace, up here, is often a quiet lie.

events.text: A pill that could raise an immortal a whole realm has been brewed in the Nine Clouds, once. The palace lords must decide who takes it. {b3_peer} has a dying master who needs it. {b3_elder} has a war that needs it more.

choices.text: Argue it should go to the weakest of you

effects.log: You argue for the weakest. You lose the vote, but the weakest remembers who spoke for them, and so does the palace.

choices.text: Argue it should be studied, not eaten

effects.log: You win them over: the pill is studied. In three thousand years there may be a hundred of them. You will probably still be here.

events.text: The Palace Lord of the Nine Clouds falls ill with a fever no pill touches. Rumour says a rival palace master poisoned the furnace. The palace master they mean is {b3_elder}. {b3_peer} begs you to prove it untrue.

choices.text: Investigate the furnace yourself

ok.log: You find it: a single grain of a bitter herb in the furnace's ash, where no grain should be. The rival master leaves the palace by morning. The Lord recovers.

fail.log: You search the furnace and find nothing but heat. The fever runs its course; the rumour does not. (-10 health)

choices.text: Brew a remedy instead of chasing the rumour

effects.log: You brew for nine days and nights. The fever breaks. The rumour dies with it, which is perhaps what everyone needed.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion has read a prophecy: a great sect below the clouds will fall within a hundred years. A buyer offers a fortune to keep it quiet. The reader who found it, {b3_peer}, comes to you first.

choices.text: Sell the silence

effects.log: The Pavilion takes the fortune. You carry the payment home and try not to think about the hundred years.

choices.text: Send a warning down, against the Pavilion's law

effects.log: You send a dream down to the sect's leader. The Pavilion suspects, and says nothing. Below, a sect begins to prepare.

events.text: Three stars in the Star Sea are lying, and the Pavilion's readings have been wrong for a century. Someone inside has been moving them. {b3_elder} keeps the star charts, and nobody else has the key.

choices.text: Find the one moving the stars

ok.log: You catch the traitor at the edge of the Star Sea with their hand on a star. They do not fight; they only ask how you knew. You do not tell them.

fail.log: The traitor hears you coming and is gone into the stars. The readings stay crooked a while longer. (-10 health)

choices.text: Read the true sky by yourself, every night

effects.log: For a year you read the sky alone, star by star. You find the three liars and set them right. The traitor is never named, but the readings are true again.

events.text: The Pavilion Master offers to read your own fate, once, in full. No one who has heard it has ever lived the same way again. {b3_peer} heard theirs a century ago, and has not spoken to you plainly since.

choices.text: Listen to all of it

effects.log: You listen. You will not repeat what you heard, even to yourself. But you sit a little differently afterwards, like someone who knows where the road goes.

choices.text: Decline, politely

effects.log: You decline. The Pavilion Master smiles: "That is the answer the stars said you would give." You are not sure if that is a joke.

events.text: A Demon Duke of the Demon Realm invites you to a feast that is plainly a test. Every seat is a fortress; every dish is a dare. {b3_peer}, a Demon Captain who owes you a fortress, sits at your left and does not touch the food.

choices.text: Eat everything and ask for more

effects.log: You eat everything. The Duke laughs until the hall shakes, and you leave with a fortress you did not ask for.

choices.text: Take the Duke's own seat

ok.log: You take the Duke's seat, and the Duke takes it back, and you take it again. By the end of the feast the Duke is laughing and calling you sibling.

fail.log: The Duke throws you out of the seat and the hall. Demons respect a try. (-10 health)

events.text: Two Demon Kings are at war, and both want you as their general. Whoever you choose, the other will remember. The first to send an envoy is {b3_elder}; the envoy is {b3_peer}, who knows you.

choices.text: Choose the stronger

effects.log: You choose the stronger. The war ends in a season. The defeated king sends you a gift every century, each one a little more poisonous.

choices.text: Choose neither, and end the war yourself

ok.log: You walk between the two armies and fight both kings, one after the other, in the same afternoon. The war ends because nobody wants to fight you a third time.

fail.log: Both kings turn on you together. You come out of it alive and wiser, and the war goes on. (-10 health)

events.text: The Demon Emperor is old, even for a demon. The Demon Realm whispers that you could take the throne, if you wished. {b3_peer} is already counting the generals who would follow you.

choices.text: Challenge the Emperor openly

ok.log: The Emperor meets you on the black bridge, and it is the fight of an age. When it is done the Emperor bows, gives you the crown, and walks into the dark with a smile.

fail.log: The Emperor throws you off the black bridge. You climb back up a year later. The Emperor is impressed, and still Emperor. (-10 health)

choices.text: Serve the Emperor to the end

effects.log: You serve. When the Emperor finally goes down into the dark, it is your hand they hold. The Demon Realm is more afraid of that than of any challenge.
